stem.text: A building draws electrical power at a rate of W(t) kilowatts, where W is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are W(0) = 2, W(6) = 6, W(12) = 7, W(18) = 3. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{18} W(t)\,dt \), the energy, in kilowatt hours, used from t = 0 to t = 18, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 6 \cdot \frac{2 + 6}{2} = 24 \); \( 6 \cdot \frac{6 + 7}{2} = 39 \); \( 6 \cdot \frac{7 + 3}{2} = 30 \).

distractor_derivations.A: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.B: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.D: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
